definitions.meaning: A part of a whole, written as one number over another: the top number counts the pieces taken and the bottom number names the piece size.
The top number of a fraction. It counts how many pieces you have.
The bottom number of a fraction. It names the piece size - how many equal pieces the whole was cut into - so quarters have denominator 4.
A fraction that names the same amount with different numbers, made by re-cutting the pieces: 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent fractions.
A shared piece size that lets two fractions be added: quarters are the common denominator for 1/2 and 1/4, because 1/2 = 2/4.

mechanismSteps: Adding fractions: pose the sum 1/2 + 1/4 - the pieces are different sizes, halves and quarters, so they cannot be counted together yet.
Make the pieces the same size: split the half into 2 quarters, so 1/2 = 2/4 and every piece in the sum is now a quarter.
Count the quarters: add the tops and keep the bottom, 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4 - the bottom number stays 4 because the piece size never changed.
Watch out: reject 2/6 - adding the tops and the bottoms pretends the pieces became sixths, but no sixth was ever cut.
objectives: Add fractions with different denominators by converting to a common denominator, starting with halves and quarters
Define the key vocabulary of fraction addition: fraction, numerator, denominator, equivalent fraction and common denominator
Explain why the denominator is never added: it names the piece size

title: Adding fractions: 1/2 + 1/4

trap.explanation: The bottom number names the piece size, so it cannot be added like the tops. The bottom number stays 4 because the piece size never changed: 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4.

workedExample: Work out 1/2 + 1/4. The pieces are different sizes, so first convert the half into quarters: a quarter fits inside a half exactly twice, so 1/2 = 2/4. Now every piece is a quarter, so add the tops and keep the bottom: 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4. The answer is 3/4 - never 2/6, because the bottom number names the piece size and the pieces stayed quarters throughout.
